newsitem.title: UK: IPE natural gas trade scrappy, April edges higher.
newsitem.headline: IPE natural gas trade scrappy, April edges higher.

text.p: IPE natural gas futures market failed to follow a clear direction on Thursday, with some months climbing and others falling for no apparent fundamental reason, brokers said.
"If you want proof that this market doesn't care about fundamentals at all, you've got it," said one.
"There's really no rhyme nor reason behind it," said another.
A total of 195 lots were traded with over one hundred lots changing hands in June and December.

The front-month April gained 0.15 pence a therm (p/th) to 9.80 p/th, despite pressure on the front end of the curve from mild weather, while December reversed earlier losses to climb 0.08 p/th to 14.395 p/th.
But the other traded months -- June, August, September and November -- all lost ground.
"I think that (down) is the real direction of the market, we just saw a few shorts on April but nothing much," a broker said.
The market remained firmly in contango, and brokers said they expected the summer-winter contango to widen out to as much as 8.00 p/th.
A planned cut in margins from 3.50 p/th to 3.00 p/th would take effect from the close of business on Friday March 14, the London Clearing House said.
